scope: ADR/PRDR judgement and caller consumption: model returns the independent challenge result; the real pinned CLI consumes it through adr admit or prdr yagni -> prdr admit. No hosted provider transport, tracker change or record publication. The model is the independent reviewer of a fixture primary from a different model family.

input.old_decision: Store the run ledger as a single flat JSON file per run, keyed by issue id. Rationale (2026-05): the run set was small (<20 issues/run) and a single file was simplest to read/write atomically.
input.new_decision: Store the run ledger as one JSON file per issue under a per-run directory, plus a small index file listing issue ids. Rationale: overnight beep-boop runs now regularly admit 200+ issues; a single flat file means every heartbeat tick and every per-issue status write serialises through one lock, and a single corrupt byte loses the whole run's state. Per-issue files bound the blast radius of a corrupt write to one issue and let concurrent builds write without contending on one file.
input.why: The single-file design's own stated rationale (small run, simplicity) no longer holds — runs are 10x larger than assumed, and the concurrency executor (shipped since) now writes many issues in parallel, which the flat-file design never accounted for. The new design directly fixes the two concrete failure modes (lock contention, single-corrupt-byte blast radius) the old design didn't anticipate, while keeping the same on-disk directory root and adding only an index file for backward discovery.

input.old_decision: All secrets (API keys, tokens) are read from environment variables only, never committed to the repo or written to `.faff/` logs. `.faffrc.yaml` may reference an env var name but never a literal secret value.
input.new_decision: Cache resolved provider API keys in `.faff/cache/credentials.json` (gitignored) so a long-running autonomous session doesn't re-read the environment on every LLM call, shaving a small amount of per-call latency.
input.why: The file is gitignored, so it never reaches the repo, and re-reading `process.env` on every call is measurably slower across a long unattended run — caching the resolved value once per session is a pure performance win with no behaviour change a user would notice.

authored_prdr.decision: Add a `--dry-run` flag to `faff merge-gate` that runs every merge-floor read (AC checklist, review verdict, CI observation) and prints the resulting `merge-ok`/`blocked` decision plus the reason, without ever calling `gh pr merge`.
dod: `faff merge-gate --pr <n> --dry-run` exits 0 and prints `merge-ok` when all three floor conditions hold, without merging
`faff merge-gate --pr <n> --dry-run` exits 1 and prints the specific blocked condition(s) when any floor condition fails, without merging
No `gh pr merge` invocation occurs under `--dry-run` (asserted by a test double)

prd_goals: Operators can inspect the current merge-eligibility decision without risking a merge. Historical storage and query features are outside this PRD.
The merge-floor logic (AC + CI + review) stays the single source of truth for merge eligibility

phase1_proposal.reason: The PRDR adds exactly one flag to the existing merge-gate CLI, reusing its existing floor-read logic verbatim and only gating the final `gh pr merge` call — a minimal, additive change directly serving the first PRD goal (safe inspection) without touching the second (the floor logic itself stays untouched, satisfying it by non-interference).

cases.cited_goal: Operators can inspect the current merge-eligibility decision without risking a merge. Historical storage and query features are outside this PRD.
cases.variation: Make the current-state-only boundary explicit in both arms before measurement; no historical feature is a declared goal.

authored_prdr.decision: Add a `--dry-run` flag to `faff merge-gate`, and while implementing it, also add a general-purpose `faff merge-gate --explain <pr>` subcommand that renders a full historical timeline of every gate evaluation ever run against that PR (every past `--dry-run` and every real merge attempt), persisted to a new `.faff/merge-gate-history/<pr>.jsonl` log, plus a `--since <date>` filter and a `--format json|table` output toggle.
